title: Ten development needs
intro:
*Five minutes. Commit before you look.*

Ten real development needs from one organization. Sort each by what it actually requires.

The test to apply: **does this work because of the information exchanged, or because someone is watching?** Information delegates. Being watched does not.

buckets.label: Needs a human
buckets.hint: The mechanism is co-regulation — a witness with a stake

buckets.label: Neither — it's not a development need
buckets.hint: The cause is somewhere else entirely

tasks.text: A new manager needs to learn the company's performance rating scale and calibration timeline before their first cycle
tasks.reasoning: Pure information transfer against a defined target, with a checkable outcome. Nobody needs to be watching for this to land, and a tool will do it at 11pm the night before, repeatedly, without impatience.

tasks.text: A high-performing engineer keeps derailing design reviews and does not believe they have a problem
tasks.reasoning: The entire intervention is getting past a self-assessment the person is invested in defending. That requires someone whose regard is at stake and who will decline to move past the avoidance. A tool that raises it gets argued with and closed.

tasks.text: A sales team has to hit a certification deadline on a new product's technical specifications
tasks.reasoning: Bounded, measurable, with a stated target — the profile from the 2022 study that actually worked. Note that this is the correct application rather than a lesser one, and it should be sold internally as such.

tasks.text: A director wants help preparing for a conversation where they will tell a long-tenured employee their role is being eliminated
tasks.reasoning: Arguable, and worth arguing. A tool can genuinely rehearse the conversation — the HRBP track builds a whole module on adversarial rehearsal. What it cannot do is hold the director's own distress about doing it, which is usually the reason the conversation gets postponed. If the block is preparation, a tool helps. If the block is dread, it doesn't.

tasks.text: Engagement scores on 'my manager supports my development' dropped in two teams, both reporting to the same director
tasks.reasoning: Module 2's card, arriving here for a reason. Nine teams, drop in two, one common director. This is a management problem and no development intervention aimed at the population will touch it — building one spends the goodwill you would need for the real conversation.

tasks.text: A first-time people leader wants to practise giving critical feedback before doing it for real
tasks.reasoning: Practice with immediate feedback and repetition is what simulation is genuinely good at, and the independent research on simulation-based practice supports modest real gains. The caution is Module 6's: the vendor claims for this category are far larger than the evidence.

tasks.text: A senior leader has been told, repeatedly and by several people, that they interrupt constantly in meetings — and nothing has changed
tasks.reasoning: They already have the information. Several people have supplied it. Applying Module 2's test: this is not a knowledge gap, and what is missing is somebody with enough standing that the cost of continuing exceeds the cost of changing. That is co-regulation with authority attached.

tasks.text: A struggling mid-level employee, low confidence after a bad year, has been enrolled in the company's AI coaching pilot as their only support
tasks.reasoning: The module's central finding, as a card. Outcomes track starting self-efficacy and hope, so this is precisely the person an unsupervised tool serves worst — and they will disappear from the data as a non-completer rather than as a failure. If you place this in 'tool' because the pilot is what exists, notice that the allocation was made by budget and never stated.

tasks.text: Twelve people need to know the new expense thresholds before the policy takes effect next month
tasks.reasoning: Information with a deadline. The only real question is whether it needs to be a module at all rather than a well-written email — which is Module 2's question, and worth asking before building anything.

tasks.text: Managers are not running development conversations, and say they do not have time
tasks.reasoning: The money test settles it: could they run the conversation tomorrow for a large enough reward? Almost certainly. So this is not a knowledge gap, and a course on how to run development conversations will confirm what they know while generating evidence the problem was addressed. The cause is what the organization actually rewards — and note the trap, because routing these conversations to a tool 'solves' it while removing the occasion Lesson 4 is about.
